details:
I propose a simple GameObject Component that allows a player to move with a surface when they are on top of it. No UDON or Stations necessary. 

There are currently multiple ways to do this in VRC, but they are all poorly performing or needlessly difficult "Hacky" compromises. You have to pick between letting your world get derailed by VRCStation's inherent (undocumented) buggy weirdness or else suffer through teleporting the player every frame and in some cases kissing cross-platform accessibility good-bye if you're also running anything else interesting in the world. 

These are the current movable platform options that world creators have:

1. UDON Platform Hook is a prefab which does this by teleporting the player every frame. The sheer volume of its use in all kinds of worlds is a testament to how much the VRCStation approach gets avoided in-practice and how badly a relatively easy-to-drop-in component for this is needed, but UDON Platform Hook also displays the limits to UDON's ability to performantly work around the gaping hole in functionality that Platform Hook fills (I doubt UDON 2 would be able to fill this gap performantly either). Resulting in awkward loss of cohesion as platforms move and Players drift away from each other.

2. Stations are a way to overcome the player-drift issue and not have to deal with the costly workaround of teleporting players every frame. And, there are many great examples of Stations being used for this out there, BUT a thing they have in common is that their implementation for this involves re-inventing existing player locomotion just to approximate player expectations (which is seems like maximizing the opportunity to have ergonomics/nausea issues if even the slightest thing goes wrong (and it's of note, MOST implementations of this get it wrong and this has gained a reputation for being a nauseating method of solving this problem)) and of course this also involves dealing with the crumbling infrastructure which is VRCStation (See post on 8 Problems with VRCStation) and there's simply no reason to push would-be world creators' patience to the breaking point with this, or making players have to define their existing comfort settings, or making players rotate awkwardly when it could just be a component. Every implementation of this is basically a miracle if it works because of the hard work of creators that have enough patience or prior experience to get it right. But this solution is like a recipe for Apple Pie where the first step (after inventing the universe) is to avoid getting injured by the swinging blades and constantly-pounding pile drivers that comprise the only baking instruments you're allowed to use in order for your Apple Pie to be enjoyable by others. The tools in this case are more obstacles than they are tools. 

Platforms that move the player are not obscure or even novel. This has historically been a fundamental building-block of video games that leads to a huge variety of gameplay possibilities and I feel that just having to explain why "Platforming" is a foundation of interactive games itself illustrates how completely absurd it is that a proposed "VRCPlatform" is not a basic drop-onto-a-GameObject component.

While I understand that VRC devs are under immense pressure to satisfy everyone and move major roadmap items ahead, I think it's worth looking very carefully at the value proposition of specifically adding a "VRCPlatform" component to that roadmap. Which is that it will dramatically lower the barrier of entry for more world creators to make more engaging, performantly cross-platform games and experiences that are currently arbitrarily completely off the table because either it requires too much effort to make it work at all, or because it cannot run performantly enough to be cross-platform. Most world creators are not going to heavily modify Platform Hook to their specific gameplay rules or spend time debugging the VRCStation-based "solution" to this. The potential value that this one component could generate simply because it completely eliminates this technical roadblock is unbound.
title: Component that makes a Game Object act as a Platform
